The present Medical University of Graz traces its origins back to the former Medical Faculty of the Karl-Franzens University of Graz, which was founded in 1863 by Emperor Franz Joseph I.

Since the enactment of the University Act of 2002 on 1 January 2004, the current Medical University of Graz (as well as the Medical University of Vienna and the Medical University of Innsbruck) has become an independent university.

Medical education had been provided here as part of a medical-surgical curriculum since 1782. In 1912, the University Hospital Graz, one of the largest hospitals in Europe at the time, was established.[5]
The university library of the Medical University of Graz was previously a part of the University Library Graz before the separation of the two universities.[5]
On 8 October 2012, the Medical University of Graz became the first university in Austria to celebrate a White Coat Ceremony of its third-year students.[16]
It consists of the university representation and the study representations for human medicine, dentistry, health and nursing science, and doctoral studies.

value.text:
The Medical University of Graz (Medizinische Universität Graz), also known as Med Uni Graz, is a public medical university in Graz, Styria, Austria. It became an independent university on 1 January 2004 under the University Act of 2002. Its history as a separate university is distinct from that of its predecessor, the Medical Faculty of the Karl-Franzens University of Graz, founded in 1863 by Emperor Franz Joseph I.

Medical education in Graz had been provided through a medical-surgical curriculum since 1782. The university's historical account also records the establishment of University Hospital Graz in 1912. Before the separation of the universities, the medical university's library formed part of University Library Graz. In October 2012, the university held a White Coat Ceremony for its third-year students, described as the first such university ceremony in Austria.

The institution's student representation covers human medicine, dentistry, health and nursing science, and doctoral studies. Its governance includes a rectorate, University Council and Senate. The reported student population was 5,110 in the winter semester of 2022/23, while academic staff numbered 92 in 2022. Its reported budget for 2022 was €296.1 million.
